transcript.content:
<issue>
Layout /tags/list.html panics on edit
See https://discourse.gohugo.io/t/hugo-panic-template-tags-list-html-not-parsed/56971

The following test panics:

```go
// Issue 14740.
func TestEditTagsList(t *testing.T) {
	files := `
-- hugo.toml --
baseURL = "https://example.com"
-- layouts/tags/list.html --
Foo.
`

	b := hugolib.TestRunning(t, files)
	b.AssertFileContent("public/tags/index.html", "Foo.")
	b.EditFileReplaceAll("layouts/tags/list.html", "foo", "Bar").Build()
	b.AssertFileContent("public/tags/index.html", "Bar.")
}
```

OK, so the issue is editing the "legacy mapped" layout names that's also valid in the new setup ...

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Hugo), find code handling "legacy mapped" template/layout names (e.g. tags/list.html mapped to taxonomy/list.html), probably in tpl/tplimpl (templatestore.go, legacy mapping). Report the code that handles legacy mappings and how templates are looked up/parsed on edit (where 'not parsed' panic could occur, e.g. a 'template ... not parsed' message). Include file paths, line numbers and relevant code excerpts.

content.content: {"summary":"Legacy layout mapping lives in tpl/tplimpl/legacy.go (mapping tables) and templatestore.go (building the lookup maps, applying them in insertTemplates, then inserting and reading the mapped templates). The 'template %s not parsed' panic is in templatetransform.go. I read the code but did not run anything, and I did not confirm exactly how a legacy-mapped template ends up with no parse tree on edit.","findings":["legacy.go:21-65: the types layoutLegacyMapping{sourcePath,target}, layoutLegacyMappingTarget{targetPath,targetDesc,targetCategory}, and the targets ltermPlural, ltermBase, ltaxPlural, ltaxBase, lsectBase, lsectTheSection.","legacy.go:85-130: the tables legacyTermMappings, legacyTaxonomyMappings and legacySectionMappings. Entries look like {sourcePath:\"/taxonomy/term\", target:ltermBase} and {\"/PLURAL/SINGULAR\", ltermPlural}.","templatestore.go:211-213: the TemplateStoreOptions maps legacyMappingTaxonomy, legacyMappingTerm and legacyMappingSection (string -> legacyOrdinalMapping). They are filled around lines 1936-1997, where the tables are expanded and each entry gets its ordinal (list position) as its priority.","templatestore.go:265: the TemplInfo field isLegacyMapped bool.","templatestore.go:1334-1420, in insertTemplates: legacyOrdinalMappings is collected per target. fromLegacyPath converts old paths. applyLegacyMapping is set only if strings.Count(path,\"/\")<=2 and the section is not partials, shortcodes or markup. The source path is looked up in legacyMappingTaxonomy and legacyMappingTerm by piOrig.PathBeforeLangAndOutputFormatAndExt(); section mappings are looked up at ~1487. When two files map to the same target, the lower ordinal wins (1402-1408).","templatestore.go:1552-1575: for each collected mapping, insertTemplate2(pi, fi, targetPath, category, SubCategoryMain, desc, matrix, replace=true, isLegacyMapped=true, s.treeMain) is called. It sets ti.isLegacyMapped=true and then calls s.tns.readTemplateInto(ti), which only reads the file content (templates.go:19-39) and does not parse it.","templatestore.go:1208-1318, insertTemplate2: it stores the TemplInfo in tree[key][nodeKey]. The line `if !isLegacyMapped { s.setTemplateByPath(pi.Path(), ti) ... }` (1310) means legacy-mapped templates are NOT registered by their original path. They are reachable only through the tree.","templatestore.go:792, in UnusedTemplates: legacy-mapped templates are skipped.","Edit flow: RefreshFiles (templatestore.go:731) runs clearCaches, createPrototypesParse, insertTemplates(include, partialRebuild=true), createTemplatesSnapshot, parseTemplates(true), extractInlinePartials, transformTemplates, createPrototypes and prepareTemplates.","templatestore.go:1630, parseTemplates: it skips any template whose state is processingStateTransformed. Otherwise it calls s.parseTemplate(vv, replace). It then looks up base templates with FindAllBaseTemplateCandidates and either applyBaseTemplate or parses directly with noBaseOf=true.","templates.go:48-53 and 76-: parseTemplate calls doParseTemplate. doParseTemplate returns early with no parse if `!ti.noBaseOf || ti.category == CategoryBaseof` (delayed until a base template is applied). Otherwise it parses ti.content into t.parseText or t.parseHTML and sets ti.Template.","templatestore.go:1889-1921, transformTemplates: for every template not yet transformed, it sets state=Transformed, skips Baseof, and calls applyTemplateTransformers(vv, s, lookup).","templatetransform.go:75-90, applyTemplateTransformers: `tree := getParseTree(t.Template); if tree == nil { panic(fmt.Errorf(\"template %s not parsed\", t)) }`. This is the 'not parsed' panic. getParseTree (92-97) type-asserts t.Template to *texttemplate.Template or *htmltemplate.Template and returns .Tree. A nil Template would panic on the type assertion instead.","Likely cause on edit: a template that is not yet transformed reaches transformTemplates without a parsed Template or Tree. A legacy-mapped entry re-inserted by insertTemplates during a partial rebuild is a candidate, because it is a new TemplInfo, goes through the delayed-parse path when noBaseOf is false, and is not registered by path. Another candidate is a template whose parse was skipped. I did not verify which of these happens."],"confidence":0.7}
